startup.name: Speko
startup.one_liner: OpenRouter for Voice AI: one API, every call on the best speech model
startup.description: A router for voice models. One API key sends each call to the speech to text, LLM and text to speech models that public benchmarks show are best for the language and use case, and re-routes when the numbers change. The founders ran the bake off by hand for four years shipping production voice for Fortune 500 clients. Four people, San Francisco, Summer 2026.

yc_acceptance.basis: Blind test: the company is already accepted to YC for its batch, so the acceptance estimate is a placeholder near certainty rather than a forecast. The unconditional prior for a random applicant is about 1 percent (0.6 to 2 percent, third party figures in yc_acceptance.md).
yc_acceptance.why_it_fails: Not applicable in this test because the company was accepted. Had it been assessed as an applicant, the most plausible reason for a no would be a thin routing layer with no clear moat against voice platforms. The founders would also need to show in the interview that they can ship quickly and have a specific first customer in mind, since YC weighs team speed and clear user need over market size.

ladder.why_it_fails: The most plausible stop is that routing looks like a feature. Investors saw Vocode and Vapi raise small seeds and then face model vendors who give their own bundles, and a router that sits between customers and vendors has little pricing power. If the founders cannot show real traffic and a margin per call, a round above the YC check is hard.

ladder.why_it_fails: Series C requires a durable infrastructure position, such as becoming the default voice gateway. Few infrastructure routers reach that scale, and the likely end is acquisition by a voice platform or cloud vendor. The records show very few comparable companies reaching this stage, and those that did had durable revenue and a defensible position, which this company would need to show well before then.

outcomes.why_it_fails: Most likely the company ends as an acquired feature or a small independent tool. Voice platforms control the customer and can add routing, while model vendors control price. Analogs such as Vocode and PlayAI exited by acquisition after a seed, and Lyrebird was also acquired, so the common path is a sale to a platform before a large round.

killers.risk: Routing is a feature that voice platforms and model vendors absorb.
killers.evidence: Platforms like Vapi already select models and vendors publish their own bundles.
killers.mitigation: Own the benchmark data and sell to enterprises that need vendor neutrality.

killers.risk: Margins are squeezed because model vendors set the cost.
killers.evidence: Routers pay per minute to vendors and cannot control price.
killers.mitigation: Charge for evaluation and observability, not just usage.

killers.risk: Benchmarks are easy to copy and customers build their own evaluation.
killers.evidence: Open evaluation tools for speech models already exist. and this was visible from the market at the batch start date.
killers.mitigation: Maintain proprietary language and domain test sets and ship new model results within a day.

technical_complexity.rationale: Calling many speech APIs and measuring them is straightforward for a small team. The hard part is fair benchmarks across languages, latency under real calls and reliability of fallback.

takeover_risk.rationale: Voice platforms have customers and can add routing in months, and the router depends on vendor APIs. A well resourced rival would need roughly the stated time and would have the incentive if the category proves valuable.

evidence.claim: Voice agent usage is growing quickly and teams struggle to choose between many speech models.

narrative.headline: A sharp but thin voice routing layer with real founder experience, likely to raise a small seed and then fight platform absorption.
narrative.general_summary: Speko routes voice calls to the best speech model using public benchmarks. The founders have four years of production experience, and voice AI developer tools have raised seeds quickly. The risk is that routing is a feature: voice platforms and model vendors can copy it, and vendor pricing caps margin. The ladder follows B2B anchors with a higher seed and flat later steps, and exits by platform acquisition are the common path. The estimates are anchored on the 2023 to 2025 B2B cohort and adjusted only with the stated reasons, keeping each step within 0.75 times its anchor. Reaching a later round years after the batch is common for companies with paying customers, and a pivot followed by a raise is part of the upside band, so the ladder asks whether a round is reached and not how fast.

assumptions: Benchmark and traction claims are founder statements.

Blind test: only the batch input file and market web searches were used; no company specific records. The seed step is read as a round above the standard YC deal of about 500K dollars within roughly 12 months of batch start.

Extraction coverage is 662 of 6,399 companies researched in the calibration sample, plus recent cohort records; later cohorts are right censored, so base rates for 2023 to 2025 batches understate eventual progress.
